dailyLessons.title: New Testament Prophets
lessonContent:
### Memory Verse
> “There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. There are differences of ministries, but the same Lord. And there are diversities of activities, but it is the same God who works all in all” (1 Corinthians 12:4–6, NKJV).

---

The New Testament church was established on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ Himself being the chief cornerstone (Eph 2:20). Through the prophetic office, God directed, comforted, and protected His early disciples.
Just as prophets guided God's covenant people in the Old Testament, the Holy Spirit continued this divine gift in the apostolic era to build up the body of Christ.
egwNotes: In ancient times God spoke to men by the mouth of prophets and apostles. In these days He speaks to them by the testimonies of His Spirit. There was never a time when God instructed His people more earnestly than He instructs them now upon His will and the way that He would have them point.—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 5, p. 661.

dailyLessons.title: Jesus as Prophet
lessonContent: Moses prophesied: 'The LORD your God will raise up for you a Prophet like me from your midst... Him you shall hear' (Deut 18:15). Jesus Christ is the ultimate fulfillment of this promise.
Christ spoke not merely as an inspired messenger, but as the Living Word and supreme Author of all prophecy.
egwNotes: Christ was the greatest Prophet that ever lived. He was the Light of the world, illuminating the pathway of redemption.—The Desire of Ages, p. 242.

dailyLessons.title: Apostles and Prophets
lessonContent: Paul explains in Ephesians 4:11-13 that Christ gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, and some pastors and teachers, for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry.
The gift of prophecy was never intended to cease with the apostles, but remains a vital mark of God's remnant church.
egwNotes: The work of the ministry is to hold up Christ before the people. In every age the gift of prophecy has been manifested to guard and instruct the faithful.—Acts of the Apostles, p. 47.

dailyLessons.title: Functions of New Testament Prophets
lessonContent: New Testament prophets fulfilled pastoral, foretelling, and forthtelling roles: edification, exhortation, and comfort (1 Cor 14:3).
They guided church decisions (Acts 13:1-3) and warned of impending crises (Acts 11:27-30).
egwNotes: He that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort. The Lord designs that His church shall be kept pure, elevated, and unified in doctrine.—Review and Herald, 1893.

dailyLessons.title: Female Prophets and Young Pastoral Associates
lessonContent: Scripture records both male and female prophets in the New Testament: Anna in the temple (Luke 2:36-38), Philip's four virgin daughters who prophesied (Acts 21:9), and early co-laborers.
God bestows spiritual gifts regardless of gender, fulfilling Joel 2:28: 'Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.'
egwNotes: God has work for women as well as for men. He chose women in ancient times and in apostolic days to proclaim His truth and minister to souls.—Daughters of God, p. 19.

dailyLessons.title: False Prophets in the New Testament
lessonContent: Jesus and the apostles repeatedly warned against deceptive, self-proclaimed prophets (Matt 7:15; 24:24; 1 John 4:1).
The biblical test of a true prophet requires: harmony with the Law and Testimony (Isa 8:20), good moral fruits (Matt 7:20), and confession of Christ's incarnation (1 John 4:2).
egwNotes: False prophets will arise and deceive many. Let all be on their guard against speculative theories that contradict the law and the testimony.—The Great Controversy, p. 583.

dailyLessons.title: Keeping Jesus and His Word at the Center
lessonContent: The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy (Rev 19:10). All authentic prophetic manifestations point away from self and toward Jesus Christ and His written Word.
Sabbath School is our weekly sanctuary to ground our minds in Bible truth and prepare to teach others.
egwNotes: The Bible, and the Bible alone, is our rule of faith. The Spirit was not given—nor can it ever be bestowed—to supersede the Bible; for the Scriptures explicitly state that the word of God is the standard by which all teaching and experience must be tested.—The Great Controversy, p. vii.

theologicalTakeaways.title: 1. Jesus as Supreme Prophet and Foundation of the Church
theologicalTakeaways.description: Across the opening days of study, Scripture establishes that Jesus Christ is the supreme Prophet who uniquely embodies the Word made flesh. The New Testament church was established on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Himself as the chief cornerstone.
bulletPoints: Jesus fulfills Moses' prophecy (Deut 18:15) as the definitive divine Prophet, Priest, and King whose authority surpasses all human institutions.
Unlike Old Testament prophets who delivered preparatory messages, Jesus delivers full divine revelation in His person and ministry (Heb 1:1–3).
The apostolic foundation and prophetic ministry complement each other to build a unified, enduring church body (Eph 2:20).

egwConnection.note: In Christ is the fullness of the Godhead bodily. All prophetic revelation throughout biblical history finds its center, truth, and vindication in His life, death, and resurrection.

theologicalTakeaways.title: 2. Functions of New Testament Prophets in Local Congregations
theologicalTakeaways.description: New Testament prophets operated within local church congregations to provide spiritual guidance, encouragement, warning, and moral exhortation. Prophetic ministry was given to equip believers, protect against deceptive snares, and foster Christlike character.
bulletPoints: New Testament prophets functioned alongside pastors and teachers to edify, exhort, and comfort the flock of God.
The prophetic gift was distributed without gender partiality, as demonstrated by the prophetess Anna and Philip's four prophesying daughters (Acts 21:9).
Prophetic messages were never intended to supersede Scripture, but to guide the church in applying biblical truths faithfully.

egwConnection.note: The gifts of the Spirit are given to the church for its protection, unity, and completion in love until the Lord's return.
egwConnection.source: The Acts of the Apostles, p. 550

theologicalTakeaways.title: 3. Testing False Prophets and Centering on God's Word
theologicalTakeaways.description: In the closing days, the lesson warns against deceptive false prophets who arise in the last days. Every prophetic claim must be tested by biblical fruit, loyalty to Jesus' commandments, and strict fidelity to Sola Scriptura.
bulletPoints: Jesus warned that deceptive signs and wonders would emerge in the last days to deceive even the elect if possible (Matt 24:24).
Disciples must test spirits according to Sola Scriptura: 'To the law and to the testimony; if they speak not according to this word, there is no light in them' (Isa 8:20).
The end-time remnant church is recognized by keeping the commandments of God and having the testimony of Jesus, which is the Spirit of Prophecy (Rev 12:17, 19:10).

egwConnection.note: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. God's Word is the detector of all error.
